title: Demobilisation at Fort Dix; contacting Dizzy
summary: At Fort Dix he met James Moody and Joe Gales and wrote to Dizzy, then went to see his brother.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, while we were in Fort Dix I met James Moody, because they were all being demobilized also. Joe Gale, a tenor player. And we became buddies, you know. We would play around in the camp, because it took us about -- about 10 days to be demobilized.
So we were fooling around, and at the same time I had contacted Diz, you know, let him know, 'Well, Diz, I'm back, baby. I made it.' You know. So --
What happened to Diz, did Diz go, or what?
No, no. Diz was here with his band. He was in New York with his big band.
He never got called up then.
No. No. No. He was lucky.

But we all showed. He told me, 'Well, Kenny, come to rehearsal at such and such a date.' He said, You'll get adjusted.' So I went home to see my brother and all that, and Carmen and I were married while I was in training.
